objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with recurrent skin lesions, recurrent infections, and failure to thrive.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—let’s get to the cause of these recurrent skin lesions, infections, and failure to thrive. Doctor: 1) When the skin lesions appear, are they typically “boils”/pus-filled abscesses, painful mouth ulcers, eczema-like rash, or blistering/peeling? Doctor: 2) Have there been fevers and unusually frequent infections (e.g., pneumonia, ear/sinus infections, thrush), and at what ages did this start?

Doctor: When the skin lesions appear, are they typically “boils”/pus-filled abscesses, painful mouth ulcers, eczema-like rash, or blistering/peeling? Patient: “They’re like bumps with pus, sometimes sore, and they keep coming back.” Doctor: Have there been fevers and unusually frequent infections (e.g., pneumonia, ear/sinus infections, thrush), and at what ages did this start? Patient: “Yes—fevers a lot, and I get sick with cough/runny nose infections often; it started when I was about two months old.”

Doctor: Given recurrent pus-filled abscesses starting at ~2 months plus frequent respiratory infections, I’m concerned about an immunodeficiency—particularly chronic granulomatous disease or severe neutrophil dysfunction; do the lesions occur mainly in areas like underarms/groin, and have any tests shown abnormal/low neutrophil numbers or very high “booster” inflammation markers?
